Params: {3: 'Metal fragments and burning splinters streak past your eyes like a shower of falling stars.'}
{3: 'You open your eyes in the real world, standing outside the simulation pod as a sharp pain tears through your head.'}
{3: 'It feels like nails being driven slowly into your skull, turning everything inside your mind upside down.'}
{3: 'At the final moment, the bridge door jammed.'}
{3: 'That tiny delay cost you your chance to escape the blast.'}
{3: 'The system severed the sensory connection the moment the impact hit, but the final instant before death—every sense pushed to its limit—still refuses to fade.'}
{3: 'A notification chimes. You force your eyes open through gritted teeth and see the number you already expected.'}
{3: 'Dying inside the tactical simulation system carries the harshest penalty of all.'}
{3: "You knew what the result would be and can't even bring yourself to care about the score."}
{3: 'All you can think about are the words that unknown woman left you with.'}
{2: "My choice wasn't wrong.", 3: '32', 4: "The score doesn't matter anymore.", 5: '32', 6: '...', 7: '32'}
{3: 'You murmur to the projection screen, the sea wind still howling in your ears.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'You remember the figure in red and white, and the certainty in her voice.'}
{1: "She isn't gentle by nature, and she doesn't hide behind pretty words. You could tell that from the way she spoke.", 2: '3', 5: '1'}

{1: 'She is a natural leader, someone who belongs on the battlefield, standing proudly in the face of danger. Yet when she spoke those simple words, they brought more than a rush of courage. They left behind a quiet, overwhelming feeling of gratitude and admiration.', 2: '4'}
{1: 'Someone had been willing to hold her fire, lower the gangway for strangers, and believe that lives mattered more than winning.', 2: '2'}
{1: 'She saw you. She believed in you.', 2: '2', 7: '1'}
{3: "Next time, and every time after that—even on a real battlefield—you'll hold to the same belief."}
{3: 'You return to the main screen and open the post-battle review.'}
{3: "The joy of being understood had briefly kept the pain at bay. Now that you've stopped moving, the shock to your consciousness comes rushing back."}
{3: 'But this is the best time to review the battle, while every detail is still fresh.'}
{3: "Besides, you can still think clearly and move without difficulty. The damage can't be too severe."}
{3: 'When you leave the tactical simulation chamber, the sky beyond F.O.S. is already turning pale with dawn.'}
{3: "Time inside the tactical simulation system doesn't pass at the same rate as it does outside. Even so, remaining connected for that long is unusual."}
{3: "The pain hasn't faded. It lingers inside your skull like broken shells left on the sand after the tide, impossible to ignore."}
{3: "At this point, you can't tell whether it's from exhaustion or the simulation itself."}
{3: 'Maybe the relentless wind in the battle had something to do with it too.'}
{2: 'Either way, I should go to the medical station first.', 3: '69', 4: 'Either way, I should get some rest first.', 5: '69'}
{2: 'Course Instructor', 3: "I've also prepared some additional material on today's topic.", 4: '1', 18: '100020570'}
{2: 'Course Instructor', 3: "It's been sent to your terminals. Take a look if you'd like to explore it further.", 4: '1', 18: '100020571'}
{2: 'Course Instructor', 3: "You're welcome to come talk to me if you have any questions. Class dismissed.", 4: '1', 18: '100020572'}
{3: 'The classroom erupts into chatter as soon as the lecture ends.'}
{3: 'One point from the lesson stays on your mind, so you open your terminal.'}
{3: 'Two new messages from unknown senders are waiting in your inbox.'}
{3: "You checked your messages that morning and there was nothing new, so they must've arrived during class."}
{3: 'You find messages with the same sender in your read folder.'}
{3: "They're the notifications related to the score review and supplemental assessment you requested earlier."}
{3: 'You thought the matter was already settled. Why would the system contact you again now?'}
{1: '"Your tactical simulation assessment score has been updated."', 3: '45'}
{2: '"Your tactical simulation assessment score has been updated."'}
{3: 'How could the score be updated? The result of that naval simulation was supposed to be locked the moment you left the pod.'}
{3: "The supplemental assessment score was final and couldn't be changed. The application rules stated that clearly."}
{3: 'You keep reading, but instead of answering your questions, the message only leaves you more confused.'}
{3: 'You check the name and student number three times. The report definitely belongs to you.'}

{3: "It isn't only the final number. Every category has been reassessed—tactical decisions, resource allocation, battlefield adaptation—and every comment is completely different from the original report."}
{3: 'The final evaluation is far above the usual range.'}
{3: "You didn't request another review. The interface doesn't even offer that option, let alone a way to submit an appeal."}
{1: '1', 3: 'No one knows what happened during that battle except the person who spoke to you through the storm and cannon fire.'}
{3: 'A warmth rises in your chest, strong enough to make you tremble. Suddenly, you want nothing more than to find the white-haired teacher and thank her in person.'}

{3: "A teacher—of course. Her tone, the way she treated you, and the authority to change the system's evaluation all point to the same conclusion. She isn't just a teacher. She's probably a combat instructor."}
{3: "But even without knowing every rule of the supplemental assessment, you understand that the evaluator's identity is strictly confidential. At least from your side, the test is single-blind."}
{3: "Combat training won't begin until next semester. Your class has to build a proper foundation in physical techniques before moving on to practical exercises."}
{3: 'Your anticipation for the course only grows.'}
{3: 'At the start of the new semester...'}
{3: 'There is still some time before class begins, and in the vast training field, the only person waiting is Adelyde, the instructor in charge of the exercise.'}
{3: "The files on the new group of students haven't reached her yet. Not that she needs them."}
{3: 'Student profiles do little more than rank people by their scores, place them in boxes, and attach labels to them.'}
{3: "Adelyde doesn't care whether those numbers are impressive or disappointing. She has never used them to judge a student's ability."}
{3: "She doesn't trust scores. She trusts what she sees for herself. That was true before the naval simulation, and it's even more true now."}

{3: "Of course, she knows the system is built around those numbers. She may refuse to use them to sort people into ranks, but she can't pretend they don't affect a student's future. That's why she once chose to change a score."}
{3: 'A distinctive mission alert sounds, and she opens her terminal for a quick look.'}
{3: 'For a F.O.S. combat instructor like Adelyde, a full semester of combat training classes is a rare assignment. More often, she spends her days traveling from one mission site to the next.'}
{3: 'The new assignment is simple and only requires her presence on-site. Even so, she requests the full briefing and plans to review it after class.'}
{3: 'Adelyde submits the request without looking up.'}
{3: "As Adelyde continues working at her terminal, the registering student's information appears on the screen."}
{3: 'She recognizes the string of numbers and looks up at once.'}
{3: "Then she hears your voice. It isn't only the numbers she recognizes."}
{3: 'In that voice, she can almost hear the waves and howling wind again. She can almost smell the salt and gunsmoke.'}
{3: 'She wants to see the face behind that voice. She never expects the sight of you to pull her into an even deeper current of emotion.'}
{3: 'You stand at the entrance in a standard F.O.S. cadet uniform, your posture straight. You carry the energy of a student, but also a calm beyond your age.'}
{3: "It's like sunlight breaking through storm clouds, a tide washing the shore clean, a lighthouse piercing the fog—and a storm from thirty years ago returning all at once."}
{3: 'You stand at the entrance in a standard F.O.S. cadet uniform, your posture straight. You carry the energy of a student, but also a calm beyond your age.'}
{3: "It's like sunlight breaking through storm clouds, a tide washing the shore clean, a lighthouse piercing the fog—and a storm from thirty years ago returning all at once."}
{3: 'Your face is still a little youthful, still carrying the innocence of your student years.'}
{3: 'Even so, the shape of your features already matches the person in her memories. One look at your eyes is enough to make her soul tremble.'}
{1: 'The person from the armory. The person from the Atlantic Eye. The person who stood at the bow of that ship.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'The person from the armory. The person from the Atlantic Eye. The person who stood at the bow of that ship.'}
{1: 'The person she searched for, waited for, and admired had always been the same.', 3: '45'}
{2: 'The person she searched for, waited for, and admired had always been the same.'}
{3: "She wants to ask if you're alright, but that's not the kind of thing you say when you've only just met."}
{3: "No. Not yet. You can't let on that they know each other."}
{3: 'She swallows hard, forcing down a bitterness that has been building for far too long.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: "...It's a pleasure to meet you. Starting today, I'll be your instructor for this semester.", 18: '100020576'}
{3: "But it isn't the first time you've met."}
{3: 'She looks at you and sees a voyage that has crossed endless years to reach this moment.'}
{3: 'For Adelyde, she has known you for a long time—since the sea burned beneath cannon fire, since the storm at the Atlantic Eye, since all the years filled with waiting and longing.'}
